title: Courses & Learning Paths
description: Independent cybersecurity course reviews and evidence-backed learning paths connecting study, official syllabi, practical observations, and original companion material.

editorial_policy.independence: Course providers do not review, approve, or determine conclusions.
editorial_policy.completion_rule: Completed records require confirmed completion and reproduced practical work. Published reviews without a confirmed completion date are labeled reviewed; publication alone does not establish completion.
editorial_policy.evidence_rule: Every review distinguishes verified course facts, hands-on observations, personal assessment, limitations, and unresolved questions.
editorial_policy.commercial_rule: Commercial relationships, complimentary access, and affiliate links are disclosed when known. Affiliate destinations are labeled wherever they are presented, and an unknown access basis is never presented as evidence of independence.

courses.title: AI Security Engineering
courses.creator: Andrey Pautov
courses.summary: An original practitioner course for securing complete AI systems across foundations, data, adversarial ML, RAG, agents, MCP, detection, DFIR, governance, and secure delivery.

reviews.title: TrainSec Malware Analyst Professional Level 1
reviews.summary: A practice-heavy malware-analysis course covering safe lab setup, reverse engineering, PE structure, static and dynamic analysis, malicious documents, YARA, and IOC extraction.
reviews.review_scope: Course page and affiliate destination verified on 2 September 2026; linked syllabus verified on 30 August 2026
strengths: Strong practical progression from foundations to behavioral analysis
Useful bridge between assembly, PE internals, and analyst output
limitations: No formal assessment or graded capstone
Written reference material is lighter than the practical content

cover.alt: 1200km Security Research neutral cover for the independent course learning record

reviews.title: TrainSec Detection Engineering Professional
reviews.summary: A practical review connecting attack simulations, Windows Event Logs, Sysmon, Elastic investigations, independent labs, and reusable detection-engineering workflows.
reviews.review_scope: Published personal review and supplied course materials; formal completion date is unconfirmed
evidence: Personal review published on Medium on 16 November 2026
Course presentation and six-scenario practice workbook reviewed
Companion guides connected to telemetry, investigation, and detection design
strengths: Clear simulation, investigation, and detection progression
Detailed Windows telemetry and Sysmon configuration explanations
Independent investigation labs and reusable incident-note template
limitations: Independent workbook has no answer key or self-check rubric
Query examples require schema review, tuning, and local validation
Formal completion date and access basis are not disclosed

cover.alt: Published Medium cover for the TrainSec Detection Engineering Professional course review

learning_paths.title: Malware Analysis Foundations
learning_paths.summary: A sequenced path from malware fundamentals and safe lab design through assembly, PE internals, strings triage, packet-capture casework, and the completed TrainSec learning record.
outcomes: Build and operate an isolated malware-analysis environment
Connect assembly and PE structure to analyst hypotheses
Perform evidence-led static and dynamic triage
Analyze malicious packet captures while preserving attribution and visibility limits
Turn findings into IOCs, YARA ideas, and defensible reporting

steps.title: Understand malware as an analytical object
Build a safe FLARE-VM, REMnux, and INetSim lab
Turn strings into hypotheses and pivots
Apply the workflow to six malicious PCAPs
Audit ten additional PCAP cases and their enrichment evidence
Evaluate short PCAP investigation stories against the evidence
Use the completed course learning record

learning_paths.title: Detection Engineering Practice
learning_paths.summary: Move from a reviewed course and attacker behavior to collection planning, isolated simulation, telemetry inspection, candidate rules, and response decisions.
outcomes: Explain the relationship between simulated behavior and collected evidence
Document sensor configuration and detection assumptions
Validate candidate logic against both simulated and legitimate activity

steps.title: Choose a behavior and map the evidence
Inspect simulation references in an isolated lab
Compare telemetry fields and collection assumptions
Develop and locally validate candidate detection logic
Connect evidence to intrusion stages and next actions
